findings.text: Configuration record holds test_driver plus test_fs as nullable text, num_threads as sizing count, test_case as selector, and test_result as aggregated outcome. Text pointers treat empty as unset, count sizes the per-thread array, and result carries the last aggregated error after a run.

Per-thread slot holds ret_sync plus fs_sync outcomes, task_sync handle, thread_idx identity, test_dev back link, and need_mod_put release flag. Driver runs use the status slot, filesystem runs use the filesystem pointer with the release flag, and the handle is cleared under protection when work finishes.

Device record holds dev_idx identity with embedded config plus misc_dev and dev handles. It carries config_mutex with trigger_mutex and thread_mutex for separate concerns, done with test_is_oom and kthreads_done plus list for progress tracking, and info as pointer to the per-thread array.

Case selector orders an invalid zero sentinel first, then a driver case, then a filesystem case, then a max sentinel last. Only the middle two select runnable behaviour; the sentinels bound validation and iteration.
Built-in default thread count is fifty.
Built-in default driver name is test_module.
Built-in default test case equals the driver case.

A boolean force flag defaults to false and two module text parameters for start driver and start filesystem default to null when unsupplied. Initialization prefers the supplied start driver over the built-in default and copies the start filesystem only when present.
Logging prefix helper prepends the module name to supplied format text.

A static registration mutex and a static integer device counter exist at file scope. No acquisition, list linkage, or counter mutation appears in these fragments, so their exact guarding role is undetermined here.
Name helper maps the driver case to its uppercase driver label and the filesystem case to its uppercase filesystem label, returning a generic invalid label for any other value.
Device conversions retrieve driver data as misc device, then resolve the containing test device from that member, with a composed helper chaining both steps from device to test device.
Completion helper increments the done counter on each worker finish and signals the shared completion only when the counter reaches the configured thread count, noting the final worker index.

Worker behavior depends on case. Driver workers request a module by configured name and store a status; filesystem workers look up the configured type and mark the slot for later release. Each worker then attempts release handling, clears its own task handle under thread protection, and participates in completion accounting.

Aggregation walks every per-thread slot under thread protection, recording the last nonzero per-slot error as the overall test result. Driver slots contribute stored status with logging; filesystem slots fail when no filesystem was resolved. A retained note records that a missing module surfaces as two hundred fifty six from the request path even though the loader itself returns one.

Single launch initializes the indexed slot and starts a named kernel thread under thread protection. If thread creation fails or yields an error pointer, the path marks memory exhaustion, logs the index, clears the handle, stores memory exhaustion in the slot status, and propagates that failure.

Stop path iterates all slots under thread protection, stopping any handle that is non-null and not an error pointer, then performs release handling for handles that still request it. A comment records that completed workers always released already, so the second step is a sanity check.

Trigger run holds trigger then configuration protection, executes dispatch, logs the stored general result, and normalizes success to zero. Only setup failures propagate as negative errors; test outcomes must be read from the stored result field, since positive values would be lost through the trigger.

Trigger store rejects immediately with memory exhaustion when the memory flag is set, otherwise runs the trigger without interpreting input bytes. It treats unexpected positive return as invalid, and on success returns the input byte count.

Bounded copy duplicates the supplied bytes with kernel allocation, reporting no space when allocation fails and otherwise returning the requested count. Driver and filesystem wrappers target their respective configuration text pointers.

Free paths clear both configuration text pointers with const-aware release and null them. The unguarded variant assumes the caller holds protection or exclusive access; the device variant acquires configuration protection before delegating.
Info synchronization frees any prior per-thread array, then allocates a zeroed array sized by thread count. Allocation failure propagates memory exhaustion and leaves the pointer null.

Unsigned synchronized update parses decimal input, swaps the new value under configuration protection, and runs a supplied sync callback. On sync failure it restores the old value, retries sync, warns if retry still fails, releases protection, and rejects with invalid; on success it returns the full input size.

Ranged unsigned update parses decimal input and rejects outside the supplied minimum and maximum before taking protection, then stores under protection and returns full input size. Signed update parses decimal input and stores under protection likewise, also returning full input size even when not all bytes were consumed.

Integer show helpers snapshot the supplied value under configuration protection and format it as a single decimal line. The thread-count show passes its unsigned count through the signed helper, while the unsigned helper has no caller in these fragments.

Configuration show locks configuration protection and renders device name header, thread count, case name with numeric id, and driver plus filesystem lines. Each text line shows the stored value when present and a generic empty marker otherwise.
String show helper locks supplied protection and renders the source text as a single line. Driver and filesystem shows delegate to it with the configuration mutex and their respective text pointers.

Typed run sets the case selector under configuration protection, with filesystem requests silently returning success without running when no filesystem is configured. Invalid selectors reject as invalid. Valid selections clear the memory flag outside protection and then invoke the normal trigger run.

Thread-limit helper has two conditional variants. One queries the loader helper limit; the other returns the built-in default of fifty. Initialization consumes whichever variant is compiled in to size the initial thread count.

Driver and filesystem stores acquire configuration protection, release prior text with const-aware free, null the pointer, copy the new bytes, release protection, and return the copy outcome which is either the byte count or a negative no-space error.
Driver and filesystem runners log case identity, target name, thread count, and identifier range from zero to one less than the count, then delegate to the shared fan-out routine.

Trigger serialization nests outside configuration protection. Run and reset paths acquire the trigger mutex before the configuration mutex and release in reverse order, preventing concurrent triggers from interleaving configuration changes.

Thread mutex guards per-thread slots, task handles, completion counting, and result aggregation. Launch initializes slots under it, workers clear their own handle and bump completion under it, and tally and stop iterate under it.

Configuration mutex guards driver and filesystem text, thread count, case selector, and stored result. Every show, store, update, copy, free, and sync path snapshots or replaces those fields only while holding it.

Fan-out launches workers sequentially over the configured count, aborting early if the memory flag is already set or a launch fails. A clean launch waits for all workers then aggregates results; any launch failure marks memory exhaustion, stops still-running workers, and reports memory exhaustion.

Trigger dispatch resets the completed count, then selects driver or filesystem execution by case. Filesystem runs require a configured filesystem name and otherwise warn and reject; any other case warns and rejects as invalid.

Initialization establishes a clean configuration from start overrides or defaults and sizes resources accordingly. On success the memory flag is clear with result zeroed and the default driver case selected; on failure the memory flag is set, a warning is emitted, text is freed, and the error propagates. Reset performs this transition under nested trigger and configuration protection.

KHO probe first attempts subtree retrieval. On success it restores and reports success or failure of restore; on a missing entry it falls through to a save path; on any other retrieval error it warns and propagates that error.

Userspace entry points are sysfs show and store handlers for configuration, trigger, reset, result, thread count, driver, and filesystem. Stores return input count on success or negative error; shows return rendered length; trigger and reset serialize through nested mutexes.

KHO test exit removes the subtree anchored at the address of the stored folio, then runs cleanup that unpreserves data folios, releases each folio reference, frees the folio pointer array, and unpreserves plus releases the folio holding the tree.

Several workers abort on unexpected case selectors rather than returning an error. Driver-only release, filesystem-only release, request dispatch, and tally paths all treat any other selector as a fatal programming error.

Initialization warns when memory exhaustion is set during setup, and the trigger store warns on unexpected positive return before converting it to invalid. These warnings signal programming or allocation anomalies rather than test failures.

Release helper returns early when the release flag is clear, otherwise handles the filesystem owner reference and then leaves the flag asserted. Because the flag is never cleared after release, stop-path sanity handling can attempt release handling a second time for the same slot.

A single memory flag short-circuits both launch and trigger paths. Once set by allocation or thread-creation failure, thread fan-out aborts before launching further workers and trigger stores reject without running until configuration is reinitialized or a typed run clears the flag.
